hard_gate_findings.gate: Ability to share domain operations across CLI/TUI
hard_gate_findings.evidence: The library crate holds profile, agent, runner, list_model, keys and text. The CLI and the TUI both call profile::load_file. All selection and filter state is in ListModel (49 lib tests pass). tui.rs only renders, decodes keys and handles signals.

defects.description: `run` can exit before its child and leave it orphaned. A thread-spawn failure after the child is spawned (forced with RUST_MIN_STACK=999999999999999, and realistic under a pids cgroup or RLIMIT_NPROC limit) panics in std::thread::spawn. catch_unwind in main then exits 1 immediately. The child keeps running (reparented), no --meta-file is written, and the exit status is not the child's. Observed on darwin and Linux arm64. This breaks §4's "waits for the child and does not exit first" on that path. `agent list` gives INTERNAL under the same condition. Fix: use std::thread::Builder::spawn and fall back to waiting without forwarding, or spawn the forwarder before the child.
defects.location: prototypes/rust/src/runner.rs (std::thread::spawn of the forwarder after Command::spawn); review2/probes/min_stack_probe.sh, min_stack_darwin.log, min_stack_linux.log

defects.description: Launcher transparency beyond the contract's 5 signals. SIGUSR1, SIGUSR2, SIGALRM and other default-terminate signals sent to the heimdall-proto PID kill heimdall-proto and leave the child running as an orphan. Under exec semantics the program itself would receive them. SIGKILL to the PID also orphans the child: there is no PR_SET_PDEATHSIG on Linux and no supervisor. Not a binding-ruling violation; it is input for the production launcher design.
defects.location: prototypes/rust/src/sigdisp.rs HANDLED, src/runner.rs; review2/probes/run_probe_{darwin,linux}.json unhandled_* and sigkill_hp_pid

defects.description: In the TUI, kill -QUIT (and other unhandled signals such as SIGUSR1) end the process by default action. The alternate screen is not left, the cursor is not shown and termios is not restored (raw mode left on, observed on Linux). §5 says "on exit by any path", but its list and K10 name only select, quit, Ctrl-C, SIGTERM, SIGHUP and panic.

summary:
The round-2 claim that the Rust prototype passes the common slice on both platforms holds up. I could not refute it by independent execution. I found no blocker or major defect.

**Rebuild and harness.** I rebuilt from source in /tmp/heimdall-review2-rust/src-copy, a different checkout path. build.sh exited 0, and all four artifacts plus the notices file are bit-identical to dist/manifest.json:

| Target | sha256 |
|---|---|
| darwin-arm64 | d9838f89… |
| linux-x64 | 28c8dee0… |
| linux-arm64 | 77d10192… |
| windows-x64 | 07b1cbc4… |

On my build the full shared harness gave exit 0 with 133/133 on darwin, and exit 0 with 133/133 on linux-arm64 (pinned harness image, native arm64). K13 holds.

**Round-1 defects re-checked.**
- **Fixed and verified:** K3a (the Linux ECONNRESET path is confirmed real); inherited SIG_IGN for HUP/INT/QUIT/TERM/WINCH; terminal takeover; group-SIGKILL orphan; FIFO meta file; FIFO profile/tui (K14); notices (all 69 linked crates, std vendored crates, CRTs); home path; reproducibility; hardened runtime; toolchain pin; O(n²); test portability (49/4/26 reproduced).
- **Honestly recorded as limitations:** SIGPIPE ignore not preserved (confirmed with a non-Python child); the early-SIGINT window (confirmed, about 0.5–1 ms); Windows pipe-server identity and WaitNamedPipe; symlinks and atomicity for the meta file.

**Beyond the harness.**
- strace on Linux shows the program executes only itself and the run child, writes only the named meta file, and connects only to the named socket. This held with TMUX/TERM set, in TUI resize and hangup.
- 38 crafted agent frames were correct on both platforms, and the client only ever sends type 11.
- My own K15 inputs stayed within bounds (≤65 ms, ≤141 MiB).
- The artifacts run without a toolchain (env -i on darwin, alpine:3.22).
- OSV reports no advisories.

**New minor defects.**
- A thread-spawn failure in run (forced with RUST_MIN_STACK, or a pids limit) exits 1 and leaves the child orphaned, with no meta file.
- SIGUSR1/USR2/ALRM or SIGKILL sent to heimdall-proto orphans the child.
- In the TUI, SIGQUIT or USR1 leaves the terminal in raw mode and the alternate screen.
- REPORT is inaccurate in places. It says std resets the child's blocked mask, but it is preserved. Its "91 crates" count is stale (117 now), and §4/§6 are stale.
- A harness defect (non-gating): the K6c SIGPIPE observation comes from CPython's own SIGPIPE ignore.

**Hard gates.**

| Gate | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Child/IPC correctness | pass (minor out-of-contract defects above) |
| Windows/WSL | uncertain (blocked: needs a native Windows 10/11 x64 host and WSL2) |
| Security assumptions | uncertain (Unix clean; Windows by code review only) |
| Distribution | uncertain (Windows native blocked; darwin ad-hoc signing only) |
| Maintained dependencies | pass |
| Licensing | pass |
| Shared CLI/TUI operations | pass |

**Artifacts.** Everything is under <repo>/tests/evidence/artifacts/g02-rust/review2/:
- conformance-darwin/ and conformance-linux/: record.json, console.log, harness_exit_code.txt = 0
- probes/: scripts plus darwin and Linux JSON/logs
- build/: build log, manifest, results.tsv, cargo-test-relocated.log
- review-summary.json

**Downloads and processes.** I added a local image, heimdall-review2-strace:1 (pinned python base plus strace 6.1-0.1 and procps from apt; not pushed), and made OSV and crates.io API reads. Nothing was committed. No processes I started remain. A running dist/darwin-arm64 heimdall-proto under /usr/bin/time belongs to another agent and was left alone.
